CORAM: HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE P SREE SUDHA  ORAL JUDGMENT This appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 challenging the judgment and award 06.12.2023 passed in MVC No.670/2020 on the file of the II Additional Judge, ACMM, Court Of Small Causes, Bengaluru, for enhancing the compensation.

sentences.text: 2. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the appellants and respondent.
The ranks of the parties are retained as per tribunal for the sake of convenience.
NC: 2026:KHC:13836 HC-KAR 3.
The injured claimant aged 13 years met with an accident on 14.11.2019 and his father as natural guardian filed claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.25 lakhs.
The Tribunal considering the entire evidence on record granted an amount of Rs.14,90,242/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from date of petition till realisation.
4. Aggrieved by the said order, he preferred an appeal and mainly contended that PW3/doctor assessed the permanent disability to the whole body as 80%.

It is stated that he sustained left leg crush injury and there was above knee amputation lower third left lower limb is 80%, but the tribunal has erred in taking his income as Rs.30,000/- per annum which is on lower side.

sentences.text: Further, contended that the amount granted under loss of income during treatment period to his parents is meager and only Rs.3 lakhs is granted towards artificial limbs and thus requested for enhancement of compensation.

5. Heard the arguments of respondent counsel and respondent counsel contended that tribunal granted excessive amount under pain and suffering, loss of amenities and future medical expenses and it is to be reduced.
6.
As the petitioner met with an accident in the year 2019, his notional income is to be taken as Rs.14,000/- as per the chart prepared by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
As he was aged 12 years at the time of the accident, multiplier 15 is to be considered.
The doctor stated that he sustained crush injury of left leg.

On NC: 2026:KHC:13836 HC-KAR examination, it was found that the petitioner has above knee amputation as per the recent x-ray of left thigh and he assessed the above knee amputation of the left lower limb as 80%.
Further, stated that he requires prosthesis and the cost of the same may vary from Rs.2,00,000 to Rs.4,00,000.
It was elicited in the cross-examination that he was not a treated doctor and he admitted that implants are in situ and petitioner was not using artificial limb at the time of examination.
If he uses artificial limb, he can do day to day activities with some difficulty.
Therefore, considering the medical evidence, this court finds it reasonable to take the disability as 80% and he is entitled for 20% towards future prospects.
Loss of future earning capacity comes to Rs.14,000 + 40% X 12 X 15 X 80% = Rs.28,22,400/-.
Pain and suffering is Rs.2,00,000/-.
Loss of amenities is Rs.2,00,000/- including future prospects of marriage.
The amounts granted by the tribunal under the other heads are confirmed as they are just and reasonable.
Further, Rs.2,86,242/- is granted NC: 2026:KHC:13836 HC-KAR for medical expenses and Rs.3,00,000/- future medical expenses including artificial limb.

7. Thus in all, components awarded by this court are as below, Particulars Amount Sl.Nos.
in Rs.
1 Loss of future earning 28,22,400 capacity 2 Pain and suffering 2,00,000 3 Loss of amenities 2,00,000 4
Medical expenses 2,86,242 5 Future medical expenses 3,00,000 Total 38,08,642

Hence,
the compensation granted by tribunal is enhanced from Rs.14,90,242/- to Rs.38,08,642/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
8.

In the result, the following order is passed:
ORDER i.
Appeal is allowed in part.
